motifs.name: multi-scale box-majority area lead
motifs.description: Every stone is weighted by the health of its chain (chains in atari, or sizeable chains with three or fewer liberties and no two eyes, are counted for the enemy instead), each empty point is then awarded to whichever colour has the larger blend of that weight inside a tight three-by-three window plus a wider seven-by-seven window around it while occupied points go to their weighted owner, and the evaluated side finishes owning clearly more points of the board than the opponent once the komi White receives is allowed for.

motifs.name: army health ledger away from territory
motifs.description: Setting territory and influence aside and scoring only raw army health - prisoners taken once the turn parity is corrected, stone mass squeezed into chains with two liberties or fewer, average breathing room per stone, finished eye points, and the share of stones reduced to crawling on the first two lines - the evaluated side leads the opponent on this combined ledger once the komi White receives is allowed for.

motifs.name: endangered-group liability advantage
motifs.description: The evaluated side has less stone material in trouble than the opponent, counting groups down to two or fewer liberties plus groups sealed inside a small enclosed area with at most one eye.

motifs.name: blocked sight-line territory lead
motifs.description: Casting eight sight lines from every empty point so that only the first stone met in each direction votes, with a weight that fades with distance and shrinks for stones short of liberties, the evaluated side ends up owning clearly more points of the board than the opponent once the komi White receives is allowed for.
motifs.source:
MOTIF_NAME = 'blocked sight-line territory lead'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'Casting eight sight lines from every empty point so that only the first stone met in each direction votes, with a weight that fades with distance and shrinks for stones short of liberties, the evaluated side ends up owning clearly more points of the board than the opponent once the komi White receives is allowed for.'

def motif(board_rows: list[str], color: str) -> bool:
    N = 19
    cells = ''.join(board_rows)

    nbrs = []
    for p in range(361):
        r = p // N
        c = p - r * N
        L = []
        if r > 0:
            L.append(p - N)
        if r < 18:
            L.append(p + N)
        if c > 0:
            L.append(p - 1)
        if c < 18:
            L.append(p + 1)
        nbrs.append(L)

    gid = [-1] * 361
    mark = [-1] * 361
    libs = []
    for s in range(361):
        ch = cells[s]
        if ch == '.' or gid[s] >= 0:
            continue
        k = len(libs)
        gid[s] = k
        comp = [s]
        n = 0
        i = 0
        while i < len(comp):
            p = comp[i]
            i += 1
            for q in nbrs[p]:
                t = cells[q]
                if t == '.':
                    if mark[q] != k:
                        mark[q] = k
                        n += 1
                elif t == ch and gid[q] < 0:
                    gid[q] = k
                    comp.append(q)
        libs.append(n)

    wt = [0.0] * 361
    mine = 0.0
    theirs = 0.0
    for p in range(361):
        ch = cells[p]
        if ch == '.':
            continue
        L = libs[gid[p]]
        if L >= 3:
            wt[p] = 1.0
            v = 1.0
        elif L == 2:
            wt[p] = 0.65
            v = 1.0
        else:
            wt[p] = 0.2
            v = -0.5
        if ch == color:
            mine += v
        else:
            theirs += v

    drs = (-1, 1, 0, 0, -1, -1, 1, 1)
    dcs = (0, 0, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1)
    dws = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.62, 0.62, 0.62, 0.62)

    for p in range(361):
        if cells[p] != '.':
            continue
        r0 = p // N
        c0 = p - r0 * N
        fm = 0.0
        fo = 0.0
        for k in range(8):
            dr = drs[k]
            dc = dcs[k]
            rr = r0 + dr
            cc = c0 + dc
            d = 1
            while 0 <= rr < N and 0 <= cc < N:
                q = rr * N + cc
                t = cells[q]
                if t != '.':
                    val = dws[k] * wt[q] / (d + 0.6)
                    if t == color:
                        fm += val
                    else:
                        fo += val
                    break
                rr += dr
                cc += dc
                d += 1
        tot = fm + fo
        if tot < 0.02:
            continue
        if fm - fo > 0.22 * tot:
            mine += 1.0
        elif fo - fm > 0.22 * tot:
            theirs += 1.0

    diff = mine - theirs
    if color == 'B':
        return diff > 5.0
    return diff > -5.0

motifs.name: parity-corrected prisoner material lead
motifs.description: Correcting the on-board stone counts by the one-move offset implied by whose turn it is, the evaluated side has captured at least one more enemy stone than it has lost, so it holds a prisoner (material) lead.

motifs.name: komi-aware dilation-erosion area lead
motifs.description: After turning groups in atari and eyeless sealed-in groups into captures, a dilation/erosion influence map shows the evaluated side holding enough board area to be ahead once the komi White receives is accounted for.

motifs.name: consolidated main framework versus scattered orphan stones
motifs.description: Welding each side stones into loose groups through contacts, diagonals, one-space jumps and knight moves that no enemy stone severs, the evaluated side keeps a larger share of its whole army inside one or two big main frameworks and a smaller share stranded in orphan groups of one or two stones than the opponent does.

motifs.name: locally besieged stone mass
motifs.description: Rating every stone by how heavily enemy stones outweigh friendly ones inside its seven-by-seven neighbourhood (closer stones counting more) and by how far away its nearest friendly stone stands, the evaluated side has clearly less of its own material stranded under local siege than the opponent has of its own.

motifs.name: wall share of contested open areas
motifs.description: Looking only at the still-undecided empty regions that both colours border, the evaluated side owns the longer healthy wall around them, so weighting each region by its size times the imbalance of the two walls the evaluated side is set to take the larger part of the open space.

motifs.name: attacking threat initiative
motifs.description: Scanning every empty point as a possible attacking move, the evaluated side owns clearly more safe forcing plays than the opponent - points where a stone that itself keeps two or more liberties would capture, atari or squeeze an eyeless enemy chain that is short of liberties, with extra credit for points hitting two enemy chains at once - so the evaluated side holds the fighting initiative while the opponent is the one whose chains constantly need answers.

motifs.name: ray-enclosure surrounded material balance
motifs.description: Shooting four straight rays from every stone and looking at which colour each ray meets first (treating a nearby board edge as a wall), a chain counts as surrounded when most of its stones are blocked by enemy stones on three or more sides, and the evaluated side keeps a smaller share of its own on-board material inside such surrounded chains than the opponent does.

motifs.name: connection integrity versus severable seams
motifs.description: Stone for stone the evaluated side hangs together better than the opponent: more pairs of its separate chains are welded by two or more shared connecting points that no single enemy move can sever, fewer of its chain pairs (especially short-of-liberty ones) hang on a single seam where an enemy stone could safely wedge in and split them, and fewer of its stones are squeezed with two or more enemy stones in direct contact.

motifs.name: ladder chase reading of two-liberty chains
motifs.description: Playing out a forced capture chase for every chain that stands on exactly two liberties - repeated atari, forced extension, intervening captures and nearby friendly stones acting as ladder breakers all simulated - a larger share of the opponent two-liberty stone mass is caught by force than of the evaluated side own, so it is the evaluated side pressed chains that can still run out.

motifs.name: chain breathing comfort share
motifs.description: Each chain is rated for how freely it breathes by adding its liberty count to the number of those liberties that no enemy stone touches and comparing that against twice its stone count, and the evaluated side has the higher stone-weighted average of this comfort rating, so its material stands in loose open shapes while more of the opponent material is jammed into cramped, enemy-pressed chains.

motifs.name: upper hand in the hottest local fight
motifs.description: Locating the single seven-by-seven sector where the two armies are in the heaviest direct contact, the evaluated side is the one winning that main battlefield, judged by its stones there, the empty points its stones reach first through the local gaps, the eye-shaped points only it surrounds, the healthy backup stones it owns in the surrounding ring, and a penalty for its own chains squeezed down to two liberties or fewer.

motifs.name: liberty dominance along the contact front
motifs.description: Comparing every pair of chains of opposite colour that actually touch, judging each chain by how freely it breathes relative to its own bulk and weighting each comparison by the stone mass of the chain that comes off worse, the evaluated side is the one squeezing rather than being squeezed across the whole fighting front once the komi White receives is allowed for.

motifs.name: efficient shape census of height, solid chains and sealed pockets
motifs.description: Judging the two armies stone by stone instead of by territory, the evaluated side owns the more efficient shape: a smaller share of its stones crawling on the first two lines and more of them working on the third and fourth lines, a bigger share of its stones welded into solid chains of five or more and into chains that still breathe with four or more liberties, and more empty points already sealed into eye-like pockets that only its stones touch.
motifs.source:
MOTIF_NAME = 'efficient shape census of height, solid chains and sealed pockets'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'Judging the two armies stone by stone instead of by territory, the evaluated side owns the more efficient shape: a smaller share of its stones crawling on the first two lines and more of them working on the third and fourth lines, a bigger share of its stones welded into solid chains of five or more and into chains that still breathe with four or more liberties, and more empty points already sealed into eye-like pockets that only its stones touch.'

def motif(board_rows: list[str], color: str) -> bool:
    if len(board_rows) != 19 or (color != 'B' and color != 'W'):
        return False
    for row in board_rows:
        if len(row) != 19:
            return False
    S = 21
    cells = ['#'] * (S * S)
    pts = []
    for r in range(19):
        row = board_rows[r]
        b = (r + 1) * S + 1
        for c in range(19):
            cells[b + c] = row[c]
            pts.append(b + c)
    D = (-S, S, -1, 1)

    hw = (0.0, -1.0, -0.3, 0.5, 0.65, 0.45, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
    nB = 0
    nW = 0
    hB = 0.0
    hW = 0.0
    for r in range(19):
        row = board_rows[r]
        for c in range(19):
            t = row[c]
            if t == '.':
                continue
            a = r if r < c else c
            b2 = (18 - r) if (18 - r) < (18 - c) else (18 - c)
            ln = (a if a < b2 else b2) + 1
            if t == 'B':
                nB += 1
                hB += hw[ln]
            elif t == 'W':
                nW += 1
                hW += hw[ln]
    if nB < 12 or nW < 12:
        return False

    seen = [0] * (S * S)
    bigB = 0
    bigW = 0
    frB = 0
    frW = 0
    for p in pts:
        ch = cells[p]
        if ch == '.' or seen[p]:
            continue
        seen[p] = 1
        st = [p]
        i = 0
        lb = {}
        while i < len(st):
            q = st[i]
            i += 1
            for d in D:
                z = q + d
                t = cells[z]
                if t == '.':
                    lb[z] = 1
                elif t == ch and not seen[z]:
                    seen[z] = 1
                    st.append(z)
        sz = len(st)
        L = len(lb)
        if ch == 'B':
            if sz >= 5:
                bigB += sz
            if L >= 4:
                frB += sz
        else:
            if sz >= 5:
                bigW += sz
            if L >= 4:
                frW += sz

    pB = 0.0
    pW = 0.0
    for p in pts:
        if cells[p] != '.':
            continue
        fb = 0
        fw = 0
        off = 0
        for d in D:
            t = cells[p + d]
            if t == 'B':
                fb += 1
            elif t == 'W':
                fw += 1
            elif t == '#':
                off += 1
        if fw == 0 and fb >= 2:
            v = fb + off - 1
            pB += 3.0 if v > 3 else float(v)
        elif fb == 0 and fw >= 2:
            v = fw + off - 1
            pW += 3.0 if v > 3 else float(v)

    if color == 'B':
        nm = nB
        no = nW
        hm = hB
        ho = hW
        bm = bigB
        bo = bigW
        fm = frB
        fo = frW
        pm = pB
        po = pW
    else:
        nm = nW
        no = nB
        hm = hW
        ho = hB
        bm = bigW
        bo = bigB
        fm = frW
        fo = frB
        pm = pW
        po = pB

    tp = pB + pW + 6.0
    v = (hm / nm - ho / no)
    v += (bm / nm - bo / no)
    v += (fm / nm - fo / no)
    v += (pm - po) / tp
    return v > 0.0

motifs.name: breadth of regional dominance
motifs.description: Dividing the board into the four corners, the four sides and the centre and settling each of those nine areas by who owns its stones and reaches its empty points first through open space, the evaluated side clearly controls more of these areas than the opponent, so its lead is spread over several parts of the board instead of being confined to one place.

motifs.name: contact-front engagement mass
motifs.description: Where the two colours meet, the evaluated side has committed the bulkier working structure than the opponent - more stones locked into large tightly packed chains whose stone count exceeds their breathing room, plus more single-gap junctions where two of its own separate chains squeeze an enemy stone between them.

motifs.name: local numerical superiority at contact junctions
motifs.description: Looking at every empty point where stones of both colours are in direct contact, the evaluated side clearly outnumbers the opponent inside the surrounding five-by-five neighbourhood at more of those junctions than the opponent does, so it fights the contact zones with local numerical superiority.

motifs.name: crowded-board settled area count
motifs.description: On a board already crowded with stones, after capturing enemy chains in atari and lifting off every group that is sealed into small pockets without two eyes, a nearest-living-stone count of what is left still leaves the evaluated side with more of the board than the opponent once komi is allowed for.

motifs.name: clean shape versus heavy clumped shape
motifs.description: Ignoring territory and life-and-death and looking only at the local shapes the two armies were forced into, the evaluated side carries fewer true empty triangles (tiger mouths excluded) and fewer solid four-stone clumps per unit of stone-to-stone contact than the opponent, and more often has a safe stone wrapped around the head of an enemy chain, so the opponent is the side that was pushed into heavy, inefficient shape.

motifs.name: careful recount of a board that looks level
motifs.description: In positions where a plain distance-weighted neighbourhood count of the whole board comes out close to level once komi is allowed for, the careful recount - chains already captured or sealed in with too little eye space erased, then each side reaching outward only through open points, stopped dead by enemy walls and discounted with distance - still gives the evaluated side more of the board than the opponent.

motifs.name: low-line pressing at contact points
motifs.description: At every point where the two colours touch, the stone nearer the board edge along the direction of that contact is the pressed one, and weighting each contact by how low the pressed stone sits (first line heaviest, nothing past the third line), the evaluated side is the presser clearly more often than the pressed, so its stones stand on the outside while the opponent crawls along the low lines.

motifs.name: outnumbered light-group liability
motifs.description: Among small chains of at most three stones that still have three or more liberties, the evaluated side owns fewer groups that are locally outnumbered (more enemy stones within two points than friendly support within three points) than the opponent does, so its thin floating stones are the better backed-up ones.

motifs.name: weakest group on the board belongs to the opponent
motifs.description: Judging each army only by its extremes - the single least secure loose group, rated from its liberties, eye points, unobstructed escape room, enemy contact and its own bulk, together with the single largest thoroughly safe group - the evaluated side owns both the healthier worst group and the bigger solid group, so the most vulnerable formation on the board is the opponent one.

motifs.name: untouched home zones
motifs.description: Sliding a four-by-four window over the whole board, the evaluated side owns more separate untouched zones - patches holding at least three of its healthy stones with no healthy enemy stone inside and at most one healthy enemy stone in the ring around them - than the opponent owns against it.

motifs.name: corner-wrap clamp advantage
motifs.description: Counting only stones whose chains still have three or more liberties, the evaluated side traps more enemy stones in an L-shaped clamp (its own stones on two perpendicular sides of the enemy stone, counted double when it also holds the enclosing diagonal) than the opponent traps of evaluated-side stones, so the evaluated side is the one wrapping around in the contact fights.

motifs.name: pressured baseless big-group liability
motifs.description: Among substantial chains of four or more stones that still have three or more liberties and no two clear eyes, the evaluated side carries less stone material in heavy groups that lack eye space and an edge base while enemy stones outnumber friendly support in their surroundings, so the opponent is the one saddled with pressured big groups.
motifs.source:
MOTIF_NAME = 'pressured baseless big-group liability'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'Among substantial chains of four or more stones that still have three or more liberties and no two clear eyes, the evaluated side carries less stone material in heavy groups that lack eye space and an edge base while enemy stones outnumber friendly support in their surroundings, so the opponent is the one saddled with pressured big groups.'

def motif(board_rows: list[str], color: str) -> bool:
    N = 19
    cells = ''.join(board_rows)

    nb = []
    for p in range(361):
        r = p // N
        c = p - r * N
        L = []
        if r > 0:
            L.append(p - N)
        if r < 18:
            L.append(p + N)
        if c > 0:
            L.append(p - 1)
        if c < 18:
            L.append(p + 1)
        nb.append(L)

    gid = [-1] * 361
    mark = [-1] * 361
    members = []
    libl = []
    eyel = []

    for s in range(361):
        ch = cells[s]
        if ch == '.' or gid[s] >= 0:
            continue
        k = len(members)
        gid[s] = k
        comp = [s]
        n = 0
        eyes = 0
        i = 0
        while i < len(comp):
            p = comp[i]
            i += 1
            for q in nb[p]:
                t = cells[q]
                if t == '.':
                    if mark[q] != k:
                        mark[q] = k
                        n += 1
                        ok = True
                        for z in nb[q]:
                            if cells[z] != ch:
                                ok = False
                                break
                        if ok:
                            eyes += 1
                elif t == ch and gid[q] < 0:
                    gid[q] = k
                    comp.append(q)
        members.append(comp)
        libl.append(n)
        eyel.append(eyes)

    seen = [-1] * 361
    mine = 0.0
    theirs = 0.0

    for k in range(len(members)):
        comp = members[k]
        sz = len(comp)
        if sz < 4 or libl[k] < 3 or eyel[k] >= 2:
            continue
        ch = cells[comp[0]]
        en = 'W' if ch == 'B' else 'B'
        ef = 0.0
        ff = 0.0
        minline = 19
        for p in comp:
            r = p // N
            c = p - r * N
            a = r if r < 18 - r else 18 - r
            b = c if c < 18 - c else 18 - c
            ln = (a if a < b else b) + 1
            if ln < minline:
                minline = ln
            r0 = r - 2 if r > 2 else 0
            r1 = r + 2 if r < 16 else 18
            c0 = c - 2 if c > 2 else 0
            c1 = c + 2 if c < 16 else 18
            for rr in range(r0, r1 + 1):
                base = rr * N
                for cc in range(c0, c1 + 1):
                    q = base + cc
                    t = cells[q]
                    if t == '.' or seen[q] == k:
                        continue
                    seen[q] = k
                    g = gid[q]
                    if g == k:
                        continue
                    lg = libl[g]
                    if lg >= 3:
                        w = 1.0
                    elif lg == 2:
                        w = 0.6
                    else:
                        w = 0.15
                    if t == en:
                        ef += w
                    else:
                        ff += w

        pres = (ef - ff) / (ef + ff + 5.0)
        if pres <= 0.0:
            continue
        space = libl[k] + 2.5 * eyel[k] + (4.0 if minline <= 2 else 0.0)
        room = 1.0 - space / 18.0
        if room <= 0.0:
            continue
        v = sz * pres * room
        if ch == color:
            mine += v
        else:
            theirs += v

    d = (theirs - mine) / (theirs + mine + 6.0)
    if color == 'B':
        return d > 0.04
    return d > 0.0

motifs.name: level-count position tilted by group health, eyes, corners and solid ground
motifs.description: When the plain nearest-stone territory count including komi is nearly level, the evaluated side is the one the finer reading favours: less weak or eyeless stone mass, more liberties per stone, more two-eyed groups, control of more corners and more territory held tight against its own stones.

motifs.name: sealed enclosed-territory surplus
motifs.description: Flood-filling the empty points into connected regions and awarding each region to the colour whose stones alone (or overwhelmingly) wall it in, the evaluated side holds clearly more fully sealed territory than the opponent once the komi White receives is allowed for.

motifs.name: capturing-race superiority in mutually boxed-in fights
motifs.description: In each local fight where a chain of both colours is boxed in with no open space to run to and neither side yet holds two eyes, the liberty race is settled by outside liberties with the shared liberties awarded to whichever racer owns the only eye and exact ties going to the side to move, and the evaluated side wins those races on balance, so more enemy stone mass than friendly stone mass is doomed in the pending capturing races.

motifs.name: living incursions inside the opponent sphere
motifs.description: Weighing every chain by how deeply it camps inside enemy-dominated surroundings (many enemy stones and almost no friendly help within three points) and by how comfortably it can live there (two eyes, or liberties plus access to a large open area rather than being sealed in), the evaluated side owns clearly more healthy stone mass planted inside the opponent sphere of influence than the opponent owns inside the evaluated side sphere.

motifs.name: settled two-eye life share
motifs.description: After the side to move lifts off any enemy chain already in atari, every empty region walled in by a single colour is measured as eye space (false one-point eyes discarded and small enclosed enemy stones inside treated as dead), chains that share eye space are welded into one living group, and the evaluated side has a larger share of its army settled with two eyes worth of eye space than the opponent has of its own.

motifs.name: level on the count but ahead on doomed material
motifs.description: A plain nearest-stone count of the whole board with komi gives the evaluated side no lead at all, yet once hard material is cashed in - the prisoners implied by the stone-count parity, enemy chains in atari with the evaluated side to move, and enemy groups sealed into small spaces with no room for two eyes - the evaluated side comes out clearly ahead.

metadata.score_definition: P(motif=True | winning) - P(motif=True | losing), preserved from the canonical discovery ranking.
